featured.title: Berlin Rent Increase: Which of the Four Limits Actually Stops the Letter
featured.summary: The Berliner Mietspiegel 2026 put the median net cold rent at 7.71 euro per square metre, and the rent letters built on it are landing now. Four separate limits decide whether yours holds up, and for most Berlin tenants the famous 15 per cent is not the one doing the work.

miniPosts.title: Berlin Bathing Season: What Stops on 15 September and What the Grade Leaves Out
miniPosts.summary: Every one of Berlin’s 39 official bathing sites carries the same top water grade, worked out from two gut bacteria over four years, with blue-green algae excluded by regulation. On 15 September the sampling stops. Here is what each shore really offers, flag by flag.
miniPosts.alt: The beach and buoyed swimming area at Strandbad Orankesee in Lichtenberg under a wide blue sky in mid-September

miniPosts.title: Berlin Parking Zones: When the Meter Stops and What the Resident Permit Covers
miniPosts.summary: Berlin runs 103 managed parking zones, and the price is the part people get right. The charged week runs from 45 hours to 105, exactly one zone charges on a Sunday, and two more switch on this autumn. What your zone actually does, and whether the permit is worth it.
miniPosts.alt: A Berlin residential street in Prenzlauer Berg with cars parked along both kerbs under bare plane trees

miniPosts.title: Berlin Museums Closed for Renovation: What Is Shut and What to See Instead
miniPosts.summary: The Pergamonmuseum has been shut since October 2023, Museum Berggruen since 2022, and the Zeughaus is a building site with no announced reopening. Here is what is actually closed in Berlin right now, which reopening dates you can trust, why the Ishtar Gate is on a far longer clock than the 2027 headlines suggest, and what is genuinely worth doing instead this week.
miniPosts.alt: The Ishtar Gate reconstructed inside the Pergamonmuseum, a blue glazed brick gateway with rows of golden animals

miniPosts.title: Berlin Public Transport for Tourists: Tickets, Zones, Prices and Validation
miniPosts.summary: Berlin public transport uses one shared ticket system for U-Bahn, S-Bahn, tram and bus. This local guide covers zones, prices, validation, BER airport trips, and the EUR 60 fine.
